_comment: Committed, reviewed absolute performance floors for the daily perf-regression
compare step (.buildkite/scripts/steps/perf-test-compare.sh). Extracted from
that script's jq so a floor can only be loosened by a reviewed diff, never
quietly inside a shell heredoc. The compare step's rolling median + MAD
absorbs noise; these committed floors are what it cannot normalise a slow real
regression below.
Each budget carries:
dir      'up'   = higher is worse (latency, CPU, heap, alloc, error rate);
'down' = lower is worse (throughput). The compare step applies a
symmetric floor for whichever direction is set.
min_pct  minimum relative move from the rolling median that counts as a
regression when there is no absolute floor (floor == null).
floor    absolute floor: the threshold never crosses this value however
quiet the recent window was. null = no absolute floor (relative
only). For dir 'up' the threshold is max(median+3*sigma, floor);
for dir 'down' it is min(median-3*sigma, floor).
min_abs  optional (default 0): the smallest ABSOLUTE move from the median that
counts, i.e. the threshold is at least median+min_abs (dir 'up') or at
most median-min_abs (dir 'down'). For a metric whose median is far above
min_abs it changes nothing. microbench_extra.*.alloc_bytes_per_op sets 0.01
(B/op): an allocation-free benchmark reads 0.00001-0.005 B/op of JMH's own
amortised allocation (a 5% band of 0.00001 B/op flagged that noise); 0.01 is
12x the widest spread seen, and catches a 16 B object on 1 op in 1,600.
Evidence: docs/operations/performance-tuning.md 'Absolute minimum move'.
gating   true  = a flagged regression FAILS the build (non-zero exit);
false = reported just as loudly but informational (notify-only)
until the metric earns a history-derived budget.
Wildcard keys 'behaviours.*.<metric>', 'microbench.*.<metric>',
'microbench_extra.*.<metric>' and 'laptop.*.<metric>' apply to every runtime
behaviour / benchmark / laptop-variant key of that shape (e.g. match_http.p95_ms
matches behaviours.*.p95_ms). Every metric a run emits MUST have a matching budget
entry here or the compare step fails closed (a missing budget must not silently
default to 'no floor').
The 'microbench_extra.*' keys are the promoted dark benchmarks (item 15b):
InboundDecode / LocalCallbackDispatch / ForwardPath / OpenApiValidation /
MetricsIncrement (and, from item 16, ResponseWrite). They OMIT 'gating' on
purpose -> non-gating (notify-only): no baseline history yet, so a flagged
regression annotates but must not fail the build. Give them 'gating': true
once each has >=10 clean runs behind it.
The 'laptop.*' keys are the laptop / central-deploy startup + footprint profile
(item 8), emitted by scripts/perf/bench_laptop.py under result.json '.laptop' and
consumed by the daily perf-test-compare.sh. They apply to every '.laptop' variant
key of that shape: laptop.*.ready_ms (docker launch->ready, in-JVM start, and
init-file variants), laptop.*.cold_ready_ms (first-ever in-JVM/init start),
laptop.*.rss_mb + laptop.*.threads (idle footprint at each --memory cap), and
laptop.*.compressed_bytes (image download size). They OMIT 'gating' -> notify-only,
matching item 8's 'notify-only for 10 runs to establish the MAD, then a 25% floor'.
min_pct is 0.25: on a laptop-startup baseline that is a wide dead band (a backstop
against a total AppCDS/warmup loss, NOT a fine regression signal), so the metrics
stay notify-only until >=10 runs of history let a tighter, MAD-derived floor be set.
They ride the FULL baseline (no methodology fingerprint of their own); they are NOT
keyed on the container image digest, which changes on every snapshot rebuild and
would reset the baseline whenever application code changes (the trap the k6 arm-set
fingerprint was chosen over image_digest to avoid).
The SAME 'laptop.*' family also covers item 17 (N parallel MockServer instances on
one host), wired NOTIFY-ONLY into perf-test-compare.sh as the .laptop_parallel block
and produced (opt-in, PERF_LAPTOP_PARALLEL) by scripts/perf/InJvmParallelBench.java
(in-JVM shape) + scripts/perf/parallel_instances.py (container shape). Compare keys
each per-N run laptop_parallel.<shape>_<N>.<metric> so these wildcards cover every N.
The IN-JVM shape emits laptop.*.heap_used_mb (used heap at N instances in one JVM),
laptop.*.total_threads (also the container aggregate across N JVMs),
laptop.*.threads_per_instance, laptop.*.tcp_sockets (held ephemeral sockets),
laptop.*.load_p95_median_ms + laptop.*.load_p99_max_ms (the per-instance light-load
latency distribution) and the shared laptop.*.cold_ready_ms. The CONTAINER shape emits
laptop.*.agg_rss_mb (summed docker-stats RSS), laptop.*.rss_mb_per_container,
laptop.*.threads_per_container (per-container live-thread median) and the shared
laptop.*.cold_ready_ms + laptop.*.total_threads. All dir 'up' (more heap / threads /
sockets / RSS / latency is worse) and all notify-only for the same reason as item 8:
no history yet, so a flag annotates but must NOT fail the build until >=10 runs let a
MAD-derived floor be set. NOTE the harness field names differ from these budget leaves
(the .java shape is camelCase: heapUsedMb/totalThreads/loadP99MaxMs...; the .py shape
is snake_case with a _median suffix: threads_per_container_median/agg_threads) -- the
compare emission block is the bridge that maps each raw field to the snake_case leaf,
exactly as serving_percore.* maps .healthy_ceiling_rps to its wildcard.
The 'tls_handshake.*' keys are the TLS/mTLS inbound-handshake cost profile
(item 14), emitted by proxy.js handshake mode under result.json '.tls_handshake'
and augmented with per-handshake server CPU/allocation by perf-test-run.sh. They
apply to every arm key of that shape: tls_handshake.*.handshake_p50_ms +
handshake_p95_ms (TLS handshake time, dir up), tls_handshake.*.delivery_ratio
(throughput/offered — the SCALE-FREE, AUTHORITATIVE keep-up guard, dir DOWN, floor
0.90) and tls_handshake.*.handshakes_per_s (raw achieved rate — dir DOWN, only a
coarse offered-rate-INDEPENDENT liveness floor 1.0, NOT the keep-up signal; see the
dedicated _comment_tls_handshake_rate below), tls_handshake.*.cpu_ms_per_handshake
+ alloc_kb_per_handshake (per-handshake server cost; null on an image predating the
jvm_memory_allocated_bytes metric, so those simply drop out), and error_rate. They
OMIT 'gating' -> notify-only: no baseline history yet, and the numbers vary with the
handshake arm (tls13 < mtls < native-absent), so a flag annotates but must not fail
the build. They ride the FULL baseline (not the k6 arm-set fingerprint) like growth,
since .tls_handshake is not part of .behaviours and the arm set is stable. The 0.25
min_pct on the LATENCY/CPU/alloc metrics (handshake_p50_ms/handshake_p95_ms/
cpu_ms_per_handshake/alloc_kb_per_handshake) is a wide dead band (a backstop against a
gross handshake-cost regression, not a fine signal) until >=10 runs let a tighter,
MAD-derived floor be set. delivery_ratio + handshakes_per_s are the EXCEPTION — they
are absolute floors (0.90 and 1.0), not %-bands (see _comment_tls_handshake_rate
below), and neither is coupled to K6_HS_RATE. NOTE the item
9a forward-proxy arms (forward_absolute_proxy / forward_connect_proxy) land in
.behaviours instead, so they are covered by the existing behaviours.* budgets above
with no new key.
The 'h2_connection_memory.*' key is the HTTP/2 per-connection heap-delta profile
(item 11), emitted by org.mockserver.benchmark.Http2ConnectionMemoryBenchmark and
merged into the result under '.h2_connection_memory' by the h2-multiplex step, keyed
by shape: conn_1x1, conn_10x10, conn_100x10 (N connections x M concurrent in-flight
streams). The figure is bytes_per_connection = (loaded heap - baseline heap) / N, with
the event log cleared before sampling so it measures connection + stream child-channel
state, not logged bodies. dir 'up' = worse (more memory per connection). It OMITS
'gating' -> NOTIFY-ONLY: no run-to-run variance history yet, and the single-connection
(1x1) figure sits at the edge of GC measurement granularity (wide spread), so a flag
annotates but must not fail the build until >=10 clean runs let a MAD-derived floor be
set. The 0.25 min_pct is a wide dead band (a backstop against a gross per-connection
regression, e.g. the class of change the 8.0.0 HTTP/2-multiplex migration warned about,
not a fine signal). SURFACED per run (no longer dormant): the daily perf-test-compare.sh
metrics jq now reads '.h2_connection_memory' and emits each shape notify-only against this
budget (name h2_connection_memory.<shape>.bytes_per_connection, bkey the wildcard here), so
a move is annotated every build but — being non-gating — cannot red the pipeline. Because
it is now read there, this key IS the budget its fail-closed missing-budget rule resolves
against on the first run, which is why the entry is committed. It is NOT `hw`: bytes_per_
connection is an allocation / heap-delta figure (a property of the code path and JVM object
layout, not CPU speed or core count, reproducible across amd64/arm64 under the same JVM),
so it rides the FULL baseline like the other allocation metrics rather than a same-instance
subset. The one-time pre-8.0.0-vs-8.0.0 comparison that answers the
changelog is run out-of-band (Docker/RSS, both server versions, identical external
client) and recorded in the item-11 report, not in this rolling budget.
The 'premerge_alloc.*' keys are the PER-MERGE allocation backstop (item 16),
consumed by .buildkite/scripts/steps/perf-alloc-gate.sh — NOT by the daily
perf-test-compare.sh (which never emits a metric of that shape, so these keys
are simply unused there and cannot perturb its fail-closed missing-budget
rule). That gate runs UNCONDITIONALLY in pipeline-java.yml (pre-merge, blocks
the PR) and evaluates each benchmark's gc.alloc.rate.norm (bytes/op) at a
PINNED representative param against an ABSOLUTE floor. It widens the backstop
beyond MatchingBenchmark (matching only) to the request-decode and
response-write paths, so an allocation regression that merely moves bytes out
of the matcher and into decode or the response writer can no longer read as an
improvement. MatchingBenchmark itself is measured on BOTH detailedMatchFailures
arms: the true arm (premerge_alloc.MatchingBenchmark_detailed.*) is the
shipped default (detailedMatchFailures defaults to true) and exercises the
MatchDifference formatting path — the #1/#2 production allocation sites; the
false arm (premerge_alloc.MatchingBenchmark.*) is the opt-out configuration.
provisional  true = this floor was NOT derived from >=10 notify-only runs
(median + 3*1.4826*MAD, the programme's budget rule);
there is no history yet for a benchmark just written.
It is instead an absolute bound derived from local
measurement with generous headroom, honestly labelled.
gc.alloc.rate.norm is DETERMINISTIC (allocation is bytes
per op, not timing — it does not depend on CPU speed):
measured error was <0.5% within a JVM and <0.5% across
JVM launches, so a floor at ~+25% cannot false-positive
on noise yet still catches a real regression (e.g. a
re-introduced double body copy, ~+44% at 16 KB — the
exact class of bug InboundDecodeBenchmark guards).
Evidence (2026-09-17, -bm avgt -prof gc -f 1 -wi 3 -i 5, pinned params).
Confirmed in the SAME image the gate uses in CI (mockserver/mockserver:maven,
OpenJDK 17.0.19, amd64 — the CI agents' arch) AND on the arm64 laptop; each
floor is seated on the CONTAINERISED (amd64) figure, since that is where the
gate actually runs:
benchmark              param            laptop(arm64)  container(amd64)  floor
MatchingBenchmark      EXACT/100/INFO   ~1,343,051     1,478,013 B/op    1,850,000 (+25% over container)
InboundDecodeBenchmark bodySize=16384      ~37,520        37,568 B/op       47,000 (+25% over container)
ResponseWriteBenchmark responseSize=16384  ~36,466        36,409 B/op       46,000 (+26% over container)
Decode and response-write reproduced within 0.5% across arch (their alloc is
dominated by the deterministic 16 KB body byte[] copies). MatchingBenchmark
ran ~10% HIGHER on amd64 than on the arm64 laptop, so its floor was RE-SEATED
on the amd64 figure (1,700,000 -> 1,850,000) rather than the laptop one — the
first PR must not be blocked by an arch the floor was never measured on.
MatchingBenchmark_detailed (item: gate the detailed-match-failure arm).
MatchingBenchmark grew a detailedMatchFailures={false,true} @Param; the false
arm keeps the base MatchingBenchmark floor above, and the true arm — the
MatchDifference -> StringFormatter path a JFR profile found to be the #1/#2
production allocation sites, together ~28-33% of sampled allocation, made lazy
by a8898b263 — gets this SEPARATE floor so a regression re-introducing eager
formatting fails the per-merge gate rather than sailing through a gate that
never ran it. Re-measured 2026-09-18 in the SAME image (mockserver/mockserver:
maven, OpenJDK 17.0.19, amd64) at the gate's pinned params, HEAD core:
benchmark                   param                laptop(arm64)  container(amd64)  floor
MatchingBenchmark_detailed  EXACT/100/INFO/true     ~2,101,126     2,096,344 B/op    2,650,000 (+26% over container)
(base false arm re-measured the same day: laptop ~1,500,410, container
1,498,006 — within 1.4% of the committed 1,478,013 seat, so the 1,850,000 base
floor still holds with ~+23% margin and was NOT changed.) The detailed arm
reproduced within 0.2% across arch (laptop vs amd64), and its 2,096,344 sits
only ~600K above the false arm — proof the lazy path is active: eager
formatting allocated a full indented diff per field comparison per candidate
and would read several-fold higher, spiking far past this floor. Seated on the
amd64 figure with the same ~+25% provisional headroom as its siblings.
GRADUATION PLAN: ResponseWrite is ALSO promoted notify-only into the daily
microbench step (microbench_extra.*), so its history accrues. Once >=10
clean daily runs exist for each of the three, replace each provisional floor
with the history-derived median + 3*1.4826*MAD bound and drop 'provisional'.
Until then these floors gate on the provisional bound (loud, reviewed diff
to loosen), which is safer than a rolling median that would absorb slow
drift — the failure mode item 16 exists to catch.
MatchingBenchmark_HEADERS_MISS_* (the SCAN arm).
With EXACT the request narrows through the candidate index to an EMPTY bucket, so
the rows above never run the per-candidate matching scan. HEADERS_MISS puts all
100 expectations in one bucket, so the scan visits every one. The gate runs it as
a second JMH invocation at logLevel INFO,WARN x detailedMatchFailures false,true
and routes each row to premerge_alloc.MatchingBenchmark_HEADERS_MISS_<level>
[_detailed]. These four floors are GATING and HISTORY-DERIVED (not provisional).
ONE RULE for every row: floor = the HIGHEST reading from a master build in the
window x 1.025, rounded UP to the next 1,000 B. Window: the gate's own
jmh-alloc-gate.json artifacts from mockserver-java master builds 2620-2646
(23 runs, 2026-09-28/29, amd64, OpenJDK 17.0.19) -- every run since c43714c57 (an
unmatched request no longer re-checks the expectations its index scan already
checked), which cut INFO from ~7.45M to ~3.11M and INFO/detailed from ~35.1M to
~13.83M; earlier runs describe old code. Later matching-path commits moved these
rows by at most ~2 KB/op. Dependabot PR builds 2622-2625 were a check only.
row                    median     highest (build)       x1.025       floor
WHY NOT median + 3*1.4826*MAD: the rows are MULTIMODAL -- each JMH fork lands on one
of a few discrete readings (a JIT escape-analysis outcome that varies per fork), so
MAD measures the common mode, not the spread. WARN reads 295,019 or 439,019 (1,440 B
per candidate) with ~0 MAD; INFO has a rare lower mode ~2.97M (build 2632);
INFO/true has a rare lower mode 13,722,451 (PR 2622) and a rare UPPER mode ~52 KB
above the common one (13,883,053 in 2621, 13,884,225 in PR 2624), which a MAD floor
(13,837,000) sits below. 2.5% over the highest reading clears every mode seen and
still catches the regressions this arm targets (~1 MB/op at WARN before ce24dc676).
IF A ROW BREACHES: re-run once. A breach that recurs, even intermittently, is either
a new higher mode (e.g. after a JDK or image change) or a small REAL regression,
possibly one that landed some commits earlier -- check the row's history across
recent builds before blaming noise. Re-derive only by applying this same rule to
fresh artifacts from code representative of master, never with an ad-hoc value.

_comment_bimodal: bimodal: on the 200 rps (and 50 rps) arms a fixed ~4-5 ms latency clump holds a
fraction of requests that varies run to run either side of 5%, so the listed p95s
read either the fast body (about 0.4-1.0 ms) or the clump (about 3.2-4.6 ms). The
draw is per arm and per run: the same image on the same instance takes either mode.
One median+MAD band over such a window flags every clump run when the window is
mostly fast, and when it is mostly clump the median jumps and the band goes blind
to fast-mode regressions. A listed metric is judged against the baseline mode its
head falls in: the window splits at its largest neighbour ratio when that reaches
split_ratio (and the lower mode has 3 runs); the lower mode keeps the usual band;
the upper mode allows its median +/- max(3 sigma, upper_band_pct) because one or two
clump runs cannot estimate its spread (the clump spans about -16%/+22% of its
median); a head between the modes is flagged. The per-mode band cannot see runs
moving INTO the upper mode, so an upper-mode head is also flagged when the upper-mode
count in the last share_runs runs plus the head is improbable (binomial tail <
share_alpha) at the metric's historical upper-mode share, the value given for it under
metrics (persisted runs since build 443). Only the metrics whose history shows this flap
are listed. Evidence and the fixture generator: docs/operations/performance-tuning.md.
_comment_alloc_bands: bands: a listed benchmark is flagged when its head exceeds median + max(3 sigma, its own
band) in place of median * (1 + min_pct). Many allocation benchmarks are near-
deterministic, so one 5% band hid real moves of tens of bytes (+16 B/op on
ForwardPathBenchmark.renderSimple in build 724). compare never lets a band widen the
threshold past min_pct, and applies it only while the window median is within
level_pct of the median it was derived at, so a level change of more than 10% falls
back to min_pct until the band is re-derived. Each band is derive-bands.py's
max(1 B/op, 4 x 1.4826 x MAD or the largest upward residual, rounded up) over the
persisted runs of builds 502-741: allocation noise comes in whole object sizes on a
few runs in ten, which a MAD of 0 cannot see. Not listed, so still min_pct: new
benchmarks, the near-zero-allocation ones, and the gating microbench.* ones (under 15
windows at their level since build 721). Re-deriving: docs/operations/performance-
_comment_g1_churn: G1 churn gate. Emitted by run-g1-churn.sh (via perf-test-microbench.sh's third JMH
invocation) under result.json .churn and consumed by perf-test-compare.sh's metrics jq.
CandidateIndexChurnBenchmark ran NOWHERE in CI before this — only run-g1-churn.sh by
hand — so nothing would have caught G1 (the candidate index being given back under
expectation churn) silently regressing.
THE METRIC. churn.alloc_ratio_index_n15000 = the candidate-index churn/static ALLOCATION
ratio at n=15,000 expectations, indexMode=INDEX, single reader thread (t=1): CHURN
gc.alloc.rate.norm / STATIC gc.alloc.rate.norm, both measured in ONE run against stores
that differ only in whether a background writer churns the expectation store. It is a
within-run A/B (the CandidateIndexBenchmark gold standard), so it cancels host/JVM/GC/
image noise and is machine-INDEPENDENT — allocation is bytes/op, not timing — which is
why it rides the FULL baseline in perf-test-compare.sh (the else-family, NOT the JMH
.config.jmh fingerprint: a fork/iteration change cancels in a ratio) and why an absolute
floor on it is methodology-independent. dir 'up' = higher is worse.
GATING with a PROVISIONAL ABSOLUTE FLOOR — the premerge_alloc.* precedent, not the
notify-only-until-10-runs default. The convention (docs/code/performance-measurement.md)
is that a metric graduates to gating once it has >=10 clean runs and a history-derived
median+3*1.4826*MAD budget. This metric takes the SAME documented exception the
premerge_alloc.* floors take: a DETERMINISTIC allocation metric (bytes/op, CPU-speed
independent) expressed as a RATIO, whose regression is THREE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE away, can
gate from day one on an absolute floor with generous headroom, honestly labelled
provisional:true — because a rolling median would ABSORB the slow drift this control
exists to catch (a metric that 'cannot fail' until it has 10 runs is no gate at all).
THRESHOLD = floor 1.5 (min_pct 0, so for dir up the operative threshold is
max(median+3*sigma, 1.5) = 1.5 while the median sits at ~1.06). Chosen from the recorded
evidence, not a feeling. Measured 2026-09-21 at the CI-mode params (-f 1 -wi 3 -i 5 -t 1,
ratio 1.071 (the plan records 1.06x +/- 3.4 B under its fuller config). Worst-case within
(a) LOOSE enough not to fire on noise: 1.5 sits ~30% above even the noisy short-run
upper bound 1.16, and the CI config's extra iterations tighten the ratio toward the
plan's +/-3.4 B, tighter still. No plausible run-to-run jitter reaches 1.5.
(b) TIGHT enough to catch the regression it exists for: a reintroduced rebuild-on-read
moves allocation ~13,000x under churn (the pre-fix figure in the G1 section), so the
ratio lands at ~1000x+; 1.5 catches it with a ~600x margin, and catches ANY >=1.5x
(i.e. >=50% more allocation under churn) — unambiguously a defect at a 1.06 baseline.
WHAT TRIPS IT: any run whose n=15,000/INDEX/t=1 churn/static allocation ratio exceeds 1.5.
GRADUATION: replace 1.5 with the history-derived median+3*1.4826*MAD bound and drop
provisional once >=10 clean daily runs exist (same plan as premerge_alloc.*). The daily
compare only gates once the global baseline has warmed up (>=MIN_BASELINE runs and >=1
comparable prior churn value); until then the row shows ':new: new', not a false pass.
_comment_info_log_level_arm: Plan open question 5 — the INFO-log-level PUBLICATION arm. perf-test-run.sh
re-measures the two PUBLISHED figure families (the knee curve and the
per-behaviour percentiles) against a SECOND SUT at the SHIPPED-DEFAULT log
level (INFO), so the site can show an honest out-of-the-box number ALONGSIDE
the tracked ERROR baseline. The owner's decision: keep ERROR for the tracked
series (a performance-sensitive user really does set ERROR, and every stored
S3 run is ERROR, so publishing it is legitimate) but publish INFO too, clearly
LABELLED as INFO, so nobody is misled. The INFO figures land under DISTINCT
result keys (.info_log_level_arm.*), so they can never be confused with, or
diffed against, the ERROR series (.behaviours / .sweep / rig_valid_peak_achieved_rps).
The budget keys below MIRROR their ERROR twins but with an info_ prefix, so a
future compare traversal of .info_log_level_arm.behaviours / .rig_valid_peak_achieved_rps
resolves against these — never the ERROR wildcard budgets. They are NON-GATING
(no `gating` key -> notify-only) AND `provisional: true`: plan open question 9
is explicit that a new wall-clock arm ships notify-only, is observed for ten
runs, and only THEN earns a history-derived, possibly-gating budget. NOTE:
perf-test-compare.sh does NOT yet emit metrics under these keys (the INFO
publication is sequenced after a run produces both series); these entries are
staged so the fail-closed missing-budget check is satisfied the moment it does.
info_rig_valid_peak_achieved_rps is dir DOWN (a throughput drop is worse); the INFO
saturation_rps knee is ladder-quantised and recorded but, like its ERROR twin,
NOT budgeted here.
_comment_tls_handshake_rate: WHY keep-up is budgeted on the SCALE-FREE delivery_ratio (AUTHORITATIVE), why
handshakes_per_s is only a coarse liveness floor, and why item 14's recorded
negative control is REFUTED. Measured evidence, Buildkite
mockserver-performance-test build 290, all three arms run in one build:
arm    handshakes_per_s  handshake_p50_ms  cpu_ms_per_handshake
jdk         51.40             6.02              8.9505   (native absent, noOpenSsl)
Item 14's control was worded: 'Force the JDK provider instead of the native one;
the handshake RATE moves.' It does NOT — and structurally CANNOT. proxy.js runs the
handshake arms at a FIXED offered rate (lib/config.js handshakeRate = K6_HS_RATE,
default 50/s) via a k6 constant-arrival-rate executor, and handshakes_per_s is the
completed-iteration rate (1 handshake/iteration). All three arms achieved ~51/s = the
offered rate + measurement jitter, INDEPENDENT of the TLS provider. handshakes_per_s
therefore measures the OFFERED rate, not the server's handshake CAPACITY, and moves
only if the server drops BELOW the modest fixed offered load. The control as worded is
REFUTED: the provider change did not move the rate.
What DID move under the JDK provider — and is the real, sensitive signal — is the
per-handshake COST: handshake_p50_ms 3.992 -> 6.02 (+51%) and cpu_ms_per_handshake
7.133 -> 8.9505 (+25%). Those columns (dir up, 0.25 band above) catch a provider
regression; a +51% p50 move clears the 25% band with margin, and the +25% CPU move
just clears it (so 0.25 is the LOOSEST defensible band for CPU — tighten toward the
history-derived median+3*1.4826*MAD once >=10 runs exist; do NOT widen it).
KEEP-UP (did the server sustain the offered handshake load?) is on delivery_ratio =
throughput/offered, computed per arm by proxy.js. It is INHERENTLY SCALE-FREE: it
sits at ~1.0 whatever the offered rate is, so a change to K6_HS_RATE cannot invalidate
it. That is why keep-up is budgeted HERE and delivery_ratio is the AUTHORITATIVE
keep-up guard: dir down, floor 0.90 (the server must complete >=90% of the offered
handshakes — the exact intent the old '45 out of 50/s' floor encoded, but with the
K6_HS_RATE coupling REMOVED rather than documented). For dir down with a floor the
threshold is min(median-3*sigma, 0.90); with a stable ~1.0 median the operative bound
is the 0.90 floor. build-290 delivery_ratio ~1.03 (cross-arm spread 0.0004 at that one
build — illustrative of how tight this metric sits, NOT the historical per-arm MAD the
threshold actually uses; that MAD will be of the same small order), well clear of 0.90,
so it cannot false-fire on jitter yet fires the moment the server falls below 90% of
offered — proven in the compare replay: candidate ratio 0.80 flags, ~1.0 does not.
handshakes_per_s is DEMOTED to a coarse, offered-rate-INDEPENDENT LIVENESS floor
(dir down, floor 1.0): it fires only if an arm produced <1 completed handshake/sec —
a dead / unreachable SUT — which is true at ANY sane offered rate, so it carries NO
K6_HS_RATE coupling either. It is a defence-in-depth backstop, NOT the keep-up
control: if offered_rps is ever 0/absent, proxy.js emits delivery_ratio = null (it
drops out of the compare via select(.value != null)), and this raw-rate liveness floor
still catches a dead arm. handshakes_per_s is deliberately NOT the authoritative
keep-up signal; do NOT 'promote' it back to a value-of-offered-rate floor (that was
the coupled 45/50 form this change replaced) and do NOT delete delivery_ratio as
'redundant' — delivery_ratio is the one that must survive.
MAINTENANCE: there is NO offered-rate coupling left to maintain. delivery_ratio 0.90
and handshakes_per_s 1.0 are both correct at any K6_HS_RATE, so changing the offered
rate (lib/config.js default, or a .buildkite/scripts/steps/perf-test-run.sh override)
needs NO budget edit here. All tls_handshake.* entries are NON-GATING (no `gating`
key) like the rest of the family: notify-only until >=10 runs of history let a tighter,
MAD-derived floor be set. offered_rps + delivery_ratio are emitted in the
.tls_handshake block for anyone auditing these floors.
_comment_path_coverage: Path-coverage arms (lib/perf-path-coverage.sh + k6/coverage.js), read from
.path_coverage.arms.<arm>. Every entry OMITS 'gating' (notify-only) and is
'provisional': the values are starting bands, not derived from run history. Once
>=10 clean daily runs exist, replace each with the median + 3*1.4826*MAD bound.
Latency / throughput entries are 'hw' (compared only against the same instance
type). p50_ratio / p99_ratio / handshake_p50_ratio are within-run mtls/tls A/Bs
on one SUT, so they are not 'hw'. Absolute floors: error_rate 2% (as
tls_handshake), delivery_ratio 0.90 (the regression delivery guard), handshakes_per_s
1/s (liveness only), persisted_ratio 0.90 (disk capture silently stopping),
dropped_ratio 0.1% of proxied requests, ring_occupancy_peak_ratio 5% of the ring and
direct_pool_peak_mib 64 MiB (both normally sit at ~0, where a relative band would flag
single-slot noise). Memory and transfer figures (*_mib, received_mib_per_s) are
binary MiB (1,048,576 bytes).
min_samples 5000 on the three p99 metrics: a p99 is judged only when its tail holds at
least 50 requests, in the head and in every baseline run. Over builds 644-732 the arms
with a 35-request tail (jsonpath_100, jsonschema_100 at 3,501 samples) had a robust CV of
0.20-0.23 and 6 of 35 runs each above 1.25x the median, while every arm with a tail of 70
or more had a CV of 0.07 or less and none. download_32mib (71 samples, a p99 that is its
maximum) is never judged; its p50 and received_mib_per_s are. The matcher arms run a
100 s measured window (K6_COV_MATCHER_DURATION) so their p99 is judged from 10,000
samples. Evidence: docs/operations/performance-tuning.md 'Tail sample minimum'.
_comment_streaming: Item 12 (LLM/SSE streaming). NON-GATING: no history exists yet, and the two
absolute/A-B metrics are measured against a DELIBERATELY CPU- and thread-
constrained SUT so the measurement sits near the knee where a regression shows.
They are therefore RELATIVE tripwires, not absolute production figures.
heap_bytes_per_stream is an UPPER bound - it includes streamed bodies still
retained in the count-bounded event-log ring, not just per-stream state.
_comment_clustered_state: Item 13 (clustered state under load). regression.js is run UNCHANGED against a
single in-memory-backend CONTROL and a two-node Infinispan/JGroups CLUSTER in the
SAME run, both on the same clustered image, and the metric is the per-arm RATIO
(clustered / control). Keyed by arm op (clustered_state.match.p50_ratio, ...). The
ratio is a within-run A/B (the CandidateIndexBenchmark gold standard) that already
cancels host/JVM/GC/image noise, so these ride the FULL baseline in
perf-test-compare.sh — deliberately NOT the k6 arm-set fingerprint and NOT the
image digest (which resets on every snapshot rebuild, the trap the fingerprint was
chosen to avoid). NON-GATING (omit 'gating'): no history exists yet. TWO KINDS of arm
share these keys, distinguished by clustered_state.arms.<op>.crosses_network:
- MEMBERSHIP arms (regression.js: match/forward/template/large..., crosses_network
false) sit near ratio 1.0 — their unlimited-Times matches hit each node's LOCAL
compiled-matcher cache and the event log is node-local, so nothing crosses the
JGroups network per request; the ratio is the steady-state cost of merely being a
clustered member. These MUST NOT be cited as total clustering cost.
- the CROSSING arm (clustered_crossing.js, op `crossing`, crosses_network true) uses
a BOUNDED-Times match whose shared-Times compareAndSet is a synchronous REPL_SYNC
round trip on the cluster (local CAS on the control), so its ratio IS the per-
request network cost item 13 was written to find. p50_ratio is the primary signal (robust at low
N); p95_ratio is present only where BOTH arms cleared MIN_TAIL_SAMPLES.
throughput_ratio is dir:down (clustered slower = lower = worse). 0.25 min_pct is a
wide dead band (a backstop against a gross clustered-overhead regression, not a fine
signal) until >=10 clean runs let a MAD-derived floor be set. The raw per-arm
latencies ALSO land in .behaviours (as <op>_clustered / <op>_clustered_control), so
the behaviours.* budgets above cover them and adding the arms resets the k6 arm-set
fingerprint ONCE (self-healing, notify-only). The genuineness proof (2-node view,
state-crossed-the-network, control-is-single-node) is enforced by the run's
clustered_metrics_present VALIDITY check, not by a budget.
_comment_pipelining_inorder: In-order HTTP/1.1 pipelining (http1PipeliningInOrder) within-run A/B in perf-test-run.sh
(lib/perf-pipelining-ab.sh): two fresh SUTs from the run image, identical except the flag,
measured back to back on the main SUT cpuset. Keyed pipelining_inorder.<arm>.<metric>, arm
one of match / forward (regression.js, never pipelined) or pipelined (a Python client
writing DEPTH requests per send on each connection). *_ratio is on / off, so dir up means
the gate got costlier (throughput_ratio dir down). The ratios ride the FULL baseline like
clustered_state.*; the absolutes are hw. Emitted only when the run proved each arm ran the
configuration it claims (.measured). NON-GATING and provisional until >=10 clean runs; the
whole family is removed with the flag in the next minor release.
_comment_file_body: FILE response body within-run A/B in perf-test-run.sh (lib/perf-file-body-ab.sh,
k6/file_body_ab.js): one fresh SUT from the run image, a FILE body and the byte-identical
inline STRING body measured back to back at a fixed offered rate. Keyed
file_body.<size>.<metric>, size 1kb / 64kb. *_ratio is file / inline, so dir up means a
FILE body got costlier (throughput_ratio dir down). The ratios ride the FULL baseline like
pipelining_inorder.*; the absolutes are hw. Emitted only when .measured (k6 exited 0, the
probe proved the bodies identical, every arm <=1% errors). NON-GATING and provisional
_comment_serving_percore: Item 18 (req/s per core for the SERVING path). lib/perf-percore.sh pins ONE
MockServer SUT to C cores in {1,2,4,8,16} and drives the sweep ladder against
it from a k6 on DISJOINT cores, one point per C under result.json
.serving_percore.points. Keyed serving_percore.<C>c.<metric>, so the wildcard
serving_percore.*.<metric> covers every core-count. rig_valid_peak_achieved_rps rides
the FULL baseline; the p50-gated healthy_ceiling_rps, rps_per_core and
healthy_ceiling_p50_ms are keyed on the sweep latency-window fingerprint
(sweep.latency_settle_s, see docs/code/performance-measurement.md 'Rung-onset
exclusion'). None use the k6 arm-set fingerprint or the image digest:
.serving_percore is not part of .behaviours, and the arm set here is the stable
{1,2,4,8,...} core ladder, not the k6 op mix. NON-GATING (omit 'gating'): no
history exists yet, and the figures vary strongly with C and with how many cores
the box could spare the client, so a flag annotates but must not fail the build.
healthy_ceiling_rps  the headline serving figure per C, computed to Finding 1's
definition by REUSING lib/perf-website-figures.jq (fed each
C's sweep as a synthetic run) — not a third copy of the rule.
dir DOWN: a drop in sustainable throughput is worse.
rps_per_core         healthy_ceiling_rps / C — per-core efficiency. dir DOWN.
rig_valid_peak_achieved_rps  max achieved over RIG-VALID rungs (client had CPU headroom,
no dropped iterations, low errors) — the degraded overload
top, same rig-valid peak definition perf-test-run.sh uses.
dir DOWN.
healthy_ceiling_p50_ms  p50 at the ceiling rung (dir UP = worse) — guards that a
throughput hold did not come at a latency cost.
The 0.25 min_pct is a wide dead band (a backstop against a gross per-core
regression, not a fine signal) until >=10 clean runs let a MAD-derived floor be
set. The PRESENCE of the profile when attempted (points-or-skip non-empty) is
enforced by perf-test-compare.sh's serving_percore_attempted gate, not by a budget.
The per-rung ladder, spread, pinning proof (available_processors), skipped rungs
and retention arithmetic are recorded in the artifact but NOT budgeted here.
_comment_serving_hw_matrix: Item 27 (throughput by hardware size). lib/perf-percore.sh in hw_matrix mode runs
one SUT per PERF_HW_MATRIX point (cores x container memory limit) when
serving_hw_matrix.<key>.<metric> with key e.g. 2c-1g. Same semantics as the
serving_percore.* entries above; the p50-gated healthy_ceiling_rps and
healthy_ceiling_p50_ms are keyed on the sweep latency-window fingerprint.
NON-GATING: runs are rare and the upper points are client-limited on this rig.
PRESENCE when attempted is enforced by perf-test-compare.sh (2e), not a budget.
_comment_serving_multiproc: Item 18 (client rig). mockserver-performance-test/scripts/multi-process-sweep.sh
drives the offered-rate ladder from N INDEPENDENT k6 processes on DISJOINT cores
(one k6 process serialises internally and cannot saturate the widened client core
pool) and reports, per process-count, the AGGREGATE client-sound throughput plus a
scaling verdict. perf-test-run.sh embeds the result under .serving_multiproc when
PERF_SERVING_MULTIPROC=true (opt-in, off by default). perf-test-compare.sh distils
TWO FLAT scalars from it (NOT a per-N wildcard family, and NOT part of .behaviours,
so the k6 arm-set fingerprint is untouched). Both are p50-gated, so each is keyed on
the sweep latency-window fingerprint (sweep.latency_settle_s, see
docs/code/performance-measurement.md 'Rung-onset exclusion') rather than the FULL baseline.
serving_multiproc_aggregate_healthy_ceiling_rps  the BEST client-sound aggregate
healthy ceiling across the measured process-counts (max of the
per-N .aggregate_healthy_ceiling_rps), each computed to Finding
1's definition by REUSING lib/perf-website-figures.jq on the
AGGREGATE offered/achieved series -- not a third copy of the
rule. dir DOWN (a drop in the achievable clean ceiling is
worse); `hw` because it is a machine-dependent throughput.
serving_multiproc_scales_with_procs  the .scaling.scales_with_procs verdict coerced
to 1 (true) / 0 (false) in compare -- a raw boolean head value
trips compare's not-numeric GATING path, so it is coerced; a
null/insufficient-points verdict drops out. dir DOWN (1->0, i.e.
the aggregate ceiling stopped rising with N, is worse). NOT `hw`:
like clustered_state.* it is a WITHIN-run min-N vs max-N
comparison that already cancels the environment.
Both NON-GATING (omit 'gating'): no history exists yet and the figures depend on how
many cores the box could spare N disjoint client blocks, so a flag annotates but must
NOT fail the build -- the standing 'never ship a wall-clock gate with a threshold on
day one; observe >=10 runs first' rule. The 0.25 min_pct is a wide dead band backstop
against a gross regression, not a fine signal, until a MAD-derived floor can be set.
The PRESENCE of the profile when attempted (points-or-skip non-empty, no rig-failure
skip) is enforced by perf-test-compare.sh's serving_multiproc_attempted gate, not by a
budget. The per-N ladder, per-process detail, CPU attribution, limited_by verdict and
the full scaling block are recorded in the serving-multiproc.json artifact but NOT
budgeted here. CAVEAT: multi-process-sweep.sh pins by LOGICAL cpu id and counts
LOGICAL cpus for feasibility; unlike the main run's assert_cpusets_physically_disjoint
guard it does not PROVE the client blocks are on physical cores disjoint from the SUT,
so on a hyperthreaded box a high-N rung can under-report the server if a client shares
silicon with it -- read the ladder WITH the per-N client/SUT CPU attribution.
serving_multiproc_scales_with_procs is a boolean coerced to 1/0; a MAD band over a
0/1 series is coarse and it is notify-only for that reason too.
_comment_serving_rw_multik6: Item 44 (the published headline). The perf-xl multi-k6 arm's p99-bounded ceiling
(.serving_rw_multik6.headline, GC-masked under the gc_masked_p99 rule). Only the arm's own
compare step (PERF_COMPARE_RESULT_ARTIFACT) sees one, so it compares against runs-perf-xl/
alone, keyed on the latency window and the headline rule (latfam). NON-GATING: the ceiling
is ladder-quantised (8k steps there), and min_pct 0.15 sits beyond a one-rung move.
